\[ f(x) = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3) \]

Now expand this factored form to find the coefficient of \( x^2 \) (which is \( b \)):
1.  First multiply \( (x + 2)(x - 1) \):
    \[
    (x + 2)(x - 1) = x^2 - x + 2x - 2 = x^2 + x - 2

2.  Multiply this result by \( (x - 3) \):
    \[
    (x^2 + x - 2)(x - 3) = x^3 - 3x^2 + x^2 - 3x - 2x + 6

    \[
    x^3 + (-3x^2 + x^2) + (-3x - 2x) + 6 = x^3 - 2x^2 - 5x + 6
    \]

Comparing this to \( f(x) = x^3 + bx^2 + cx + d \), the coefficient of \( x^2 \) is \( -2 \), so \( b = -2 \).

Final answer: \(\boldsymbol{-2}\)
